original_question: Let X1 and X2 be cubic fourfolds. If there is an equivalence Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) between their Kuznetsov components, does it follow that X1 and X2 are birational?
target_in_paper: Question 7.8 (Huybrechts): the Birational Categorical Torelli question for cubic fourfolds.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target almost verbatim: it considers two cubic fourfolds X1 and X2, asks for an equivalence Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) of their Kuznetsov components, and asks whether this forces birationality. It also correctly does not impose compatibility with degree-shift functors, because adding that hypothesis would turn the question into the neighboring isomorphism statement of Theorem 7.7 rather than the open birational problem.
missing_details: State explicitly that a cubic fourfold is a smooth cubic hypersurface in P^5 over an algebraically closed field K; in the cubic-fourfold setup the paper assumes char(K) != 2.
Define the Kuznetsov component by the semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X)=<Ku(X), O_X, O_X(H), O_X(2H)>, where H is the hyperplane class.
Specify that the map Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) is an exact equivalence of admissible/triangulated categories.

To mirror the nearby context faithfully, say explicitly that no compatibility with the degree-shift autoequivalences O_{X_i} is being assumed; that extra hypothesis is exactly what appears in Theorem 7.7 to recover isomorphism.

If one wants maximal paper-faithfulness, note that no separate Fourier-Mukai-type hypothesis is needed in this cubic-fourfold setting, because Proposition 3.15 says Question 2.7 has a positive answer for Ku(X).
refined_question: Let X1 and X2 be smooth cubic hypersurfaces in P^5 over an algebraically closed field K with char(K) != 2, and let Ku(X_i) be the Kuznetsov component defined by the semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X_i)=<Ku(X_i), O_{X_i}, O_{X_i}(H_i), O_{X_i}(2H_i)>. If there exists an exact equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2), without assuming that Phi commutes with the degree-shift autoequivalences O_{X_i}, must X1 and X2 be birational?
justification: This is exactly the official open problem stated in Section 7.2 as Question 7.8. The paper first formulates the general Birational Categorical Torelli problem in the Introduction and then specializes it to cubic fourfolds in Question 7.8. The immediately preceding Theorem 7.7 explains the nearby boundary of the problem: if an equivalence of Kuznetsov components commutes with the degree-shift functors, then one gets X1 ≅ X2, so the natural next question is whether dropping that compatibility still forces at least birationality. Section 3.4 supplies the precise cubic-fourfold notation and definition of Ku(X), and Proposition 3.15 shows that in this setting one does not need to add a separate Fourier-Mukai-type assumption. Remark 7.9 further shows that the converse implication is not intended as part of the question.
